items.title: 삼성전자, JEDEC서 “AI 메모리 표준화 한계” 토로

items.title: HMM, 컨테이너선 투자에 2.2조원 투입…"선대 경쟁력 확보"
items.snippet: HMM[011200]이 컨테이너선에 2조원이 넘는 자금을 투입한다.HMM은 15일 이사회를 열고 컨테이너 신조선 발주와 리세일(신조 인도 전 재판매되는 중고 선박) 신조선 매입에 2조1천678억원을 투자하는 계획을 결의했다고 공시했다.HMM은 이를 통해 1만3천TEU 컨테이너선 8척을 발주하고, 리세일 2천800TEU 컨테이너선 3척과 1천700TEU 컨테이너선 1척을 매입한다고 밝혔다.투자 목적은 컨테이너선 투자를 통한 선대 경쟁력 확보라고 명시했다.선박의 최종 인도 예정 시기는 오는 2029년 말이 될 예정이다.ebyun@yn

items.title: '역대 분기 최대 매출' 대한항공…영업이익도 두자릿수 성장(종합)

items.title: 다올證 전2대주주, 검찰 증거 제시방식에 이의…"인수 관심 없었다"
items.snippet: 다올투자증권의 전 2대주주 측이 검사 신문 과정에서 편집된 증거에 대해 반발했다.18일 서울남부지방법원 대법정에서 자본시장법 위반을 혐의로 기소된 김기수 전 프레스투자자문 대표와 그의 아들 김용진, 프레스토투자자문 법인, 순수에셋 등 피고인에 대한 10차 공판이 열렸다.이날 공판에서는 지난 2023년 4월 최초로 피고인이 다올투자증권 주식을 매수한 경위에 대한 피고인 신문이 진행됐다. 피고인은 당시 경영권 인수 목적을 숨긴 채 지분을 매입한 혐의를 받고 있다.검사 측은 피고인이 회사 직원을 통해 다올투자증권을 포함한 수십 개 증권

items.title: 아이언디바이스, 온디바이스 AI 연산 모듈 만든다...로봇 손에 탑재

items.title: [코스피 급락] 윤지호 "단기 진통 불가피…저점매수 기회 저울질할 때"

items.title: [코스피 급락] 성상현 전무 "과매도 국면…분할매수 매력적 구간"

items.title: [증시-마감] 하루 만에 코스피 5,500선까지 후퇴…증시 덮친 '검은 목요일'

items.title: HD현대重, 중동서 6천258억 규모 VLGC 4척 수주 따내
items.snippet: HD현대중공업[329180]이 중동 소재 선사로부터 초대형 가스운반선(VLGC) 4척을 건조하는 계약을 체결했다고 15일 공시했다.계약 금액은 6천258억원으로, 지난해 연결 기준 매출의 3.56%에 해당한다.계약 기간은 이달 14일부터 2030년 6월 30일까지다. 대금은 공사 진척에 따라 지급받는다.ebyun@yna.co.kr

items.title: 증시 급락에 '빚투' 청산 압력 가중…반대매매 900억 육박

items.title: [코스피 급락] 신영證 김학균 "저평가 구간 진입…고금리 버틸 종목 가려야"

items.title: [코스피 급락] 나신평 "증권사 신용공여 리스크 글쎄…개별사 관리 관건"

items.title: 증시 대폭락에 금융당국 긴급회의…"비상대응 준비"

items.title: 이마트, 758억원 규모 자기주식 소각 결정

items.snippet: 가상자산 과세를 2년 늦추는 법안이 여당에서도 처음으로 발의됐습니다.오늘(15일) 가상자산업계에 따르면 더불어민주당 박민규 의원은 가상자산소득 과세 시행일을 내년에서 사실상 2029년으로 늦추는 취지의 법안을 대표 발의했습니다.박 의원이 발의한 소득세법 일부개정법률안은 국가 간 가상자산 거래정보가 최초로 교환된 연도로부터 2년 뒤 1월 1일로 변경하는 내용입니다.경제협력개발기구(OECD)의 암호화자산 자동정보교환체계(CARF)에 따라 국가 간 가상자산 거래정보 교환이 내년으로 예정된 상황입니다.개정안은 "가상자산 과세를 위한 거래정보 확보와 과세 인프라 구축이 충분하지 않은 상황에서 제도를 시행하면 과세 실효성이 떨어지..

items.title: 李, 임광현 비서실장에 임명장…강훈식엔 공로패
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 15일 오전 임광현 신임 비서실장에게 임명장을 수여했다고 강유정 청와대 수석대변인이 언론 공지를 통해 밝혔다.아울러 강훈식 초대 비서실장에게 공로패를 수여했다.이 대통령은 강 전 실장이 사의를 표명한 지 23일 만인 전날 임광현 실장을 임명했다.충남 홍성 출신인 임 실장은 행정고시 38회로 공직 생활을 시작해 노무현 정부 경제정책비서관실 행정관, 국세청 차장 등을 지냈다. 조사국장만 6차례 맡은, 국세청 내 대표적인 조사 전문가로 꼽힌다. 22대 국회의원 선거에서 당시 더불어민주당 대표였던 이 대통령이 직접 영입해 민주당 비례대표로 당선된 뒤 지난해 7월 의원직을 내려놓고 이재명 정부 첫 국세청장을 지냈다. 임 실장의 부인은 이경은 주휴스턴 총영사, 처남은 이 대통령 대장동 사건 변호를 맡았던 이승엽 변호사다.

items.snippet: 정부가 출산율을 높이는 데 집중했던 기존 인구 정책을 초고령 사회에 적응하고 국민 삶의 질을 높이는 종합 전략으로 전환한다고 밝혔다. 합계출산율을 올리겠다는 목표 대신 지난해 71.8%였던 경제활동 참가율을 2030년 74%로 높이겠다는 목표 등을 제시했다.

items.title: “딸 위험” 엄마 경고 무시한 경찰… 아빠·4세 아이 결국 숨진채 발견
items.snippet: 아내와 양육권 분쟁을 벌이던 40대 남성이 제주에서 네 살 딸과 함께 숨진 채 발견됐다. 아내는 열흘 전 경찰에 “딸이 위험하다”고 알렸지만 경찰은 정식 사건으로 접수하지 않고 단순 민원으로 처리했다. 14일 제주경찰청 등에 따르면, 지난 12일 오후 6시 8분쯤 제주 서귀포시 표선면의 한 공영 주차장에 주차된 렌터카 안에서 40대 A씨와 네 살 딸이 숨진 채 발견됐다. 차 안에서는 스스로 목숨을 끊은 흔적이 나왔다.

items.title: 강선우, 김경에 “원하는 공천 면접 질문, 김병기에 보내라” 말해
items.snippet: 2022년 제8회 지방선거 시의원 공천 대가로 1억원을 받은 혐의로 기소된 무소속 강선우(서울 강서갑) 의원이 14일 서울중앙지법 형사1단독 이춘근 부장판사 심리로 열린 1심에서 징역 2년 6개월을 선고받고 법정 구속됐다. 지난달 22일 보석으로 풀려난 지 3주 만에 다시 구속된 것이다. 이 부장판사는 판결문에 강 의원이 자기에게 돈을 준 김경(전 서울시의원)씨에게 “공천 면접에서 받고 싶은 질문을 김병기 의원에게 미리 보내라”고 했다고 적시했다. 김병기 의원은 당시 더불어민주당 서울시당 공천관리위원회 간사였다. 강 의원의 공천 비위 사건은 강 의원이 김씨 문제를 김 의원과 상의하는 녹음 파일이 공개되면서 시작됐다.

items.title: 흉기 난동범 “병원 무좀 치료 불만… 뉴스거리 만들려고 범행 결심”
items.snippet: 지난 13일 인천 상가 푸드코트에서 ‘흉기 난동’을 벌인 A(59)씨가 경찰에서 “병원 치료에 대한 불만을 알리기 위해 뉴스거리를 만들어야겠다고 생각했다”고 진술한 것으로 14일 확인됐다. “나보다 힘없어 보이는 사람을 (범행 대상으로) 골랐다”고도 했다.

items.title: 울주군 화학제품 공장 화재… 7000명 대피
items.snippet: 14일 울산 울주군 온산읍의 한 화학제품 제조업체에서 불이 나 시커먼 연기가 치솟고 있다. 소방대원들이 물을 뿌리며 불길을 잡고 있다. 이날 오전 9시 41분쯤 발생한 불은 약 4시간 만에 꺼졌다. 저장 탱크 33기 중 7기가 불탔다. 인명 피해는 없었으나 주변 공장 작업자 등 7000여 명이 대피했다. 당시 업체에서는 인화성 물질인 톨루엔을 드럼통에 옮기는 작업을 하고 있었다고 한다.

items.title: 출근길 서울 버스전용차로에 ‘급행’ 달린다
items.snippet: 서울 시내 버스중앙차로(중앙버스전용차로)에 주요 정류장만 골라 서는 ‘급행버스’가 처음 도입된다. 2004년 버스중앙차로가 생긴 지 22년 만이다. 중앙차로에 버스가 몰리면서 운행 속도가 일반차로 수준까지 떨어지자 급행버스를 투입하는 실험을 시작하는 것이다. 혼잡 문제가 심각한 지하철 9호선은 출근길 급행열차 운행을 늘린다.

items.title: “휴직한 김대리 올해 의대 갔대”
items.snippet: 37세 김모씨는 재작년 회사를 휴직하고 1년간 수능을 준비했다. 서울대 공대를 졸업하고 안정적인 공기업에 취직했지만, 오르지 않는 연봉에 더는 미래가 보이지 않자 의대에 가기로 마음먹은 것이다. 김씨는 결국 작년 초 졸업한 지 17년 만에 지방 한 사립대 의대에 들어갔다. 그는 “요즘 공부 잘하는 사람들이 다 의대를 가고 싶어 하는데, 나도 공부를 잘했었으니까 한 번 도전해보자는 생각이 들었다”며 “직장 다니다가 온 동기가 10명은 넘는 것 같다”고 했다.

items.title: 60대 일자리 20만개 늘 때, 20대는 5만개 줄었다
items.snippet: 3년 전 서울의 한 명문대를 졸업한 A(27)씨는 그동안 두 차례 기업 인턴을 거치고 프리랜서로도 일하며 경험을 쌓았다. 하지만 아직까지 정규직 일자리를 구하지 못했다고 한다. 그는 “채용 사이트를 보면 나 같은 ‘신입’ 자리는 거의 없고 경력직 공고가 대부분”이라며 “이제는 인턴 자리도 구하기 어려워지고 있다”고 했다.

items.title: 국내 첫 자연번식한 레서판다 마루와 마롱이
items.snippet: 14일 경기 과천시 서울대공원에서 자연 번식에 성공한 레서판다 쌍둥이 남매 ‘마루’와 ‘마롱’이 관람객들을 바라보고 있다. 이들 남매가 일반에 공개된 건 이날이 처음이다. 멸종 위기 동물인 레서판다는 암컷의 가임 기간이 1년에 2~3일에 불과해 자연 번식이 까다로운 것으로 알려졌다. 서울대공원은 2023년 해외에서 아빠 ‘라비’와 엄마 ‘리안’을 들여와 3년 만인 지난 6월 19일 국내 최초로 자연 번식에 성공했다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [뉴스 속의 한국사] 왕의 집무실 겸 생활공간… 샹들리에·카펫도 갖췄대요
items.snippet: 국가유산청 궁능유적본부가 20일부터 31일까지(일·월요일 제외) 하루 두 차례 창덕궁 희정당(熙政堂)과 대조전(大造殿)을 개방하는 행사를 한다고 밝혔어요. 이 두 건물은 왕과 왕비의 생활·집무 공간이었어요. 오늘은 희정당이라는 독특한 궁궐 건물에 대해 이야기하고자 합니다. 지난 7~11일 궁중문화축전을 맞아 공예 전시와 함께 개방돼 많은 사람이 찾았던 곳이기도 한데, ‘만약 조선 왕조가 멸망하지 않고 지속됐더라면 모든 궁궐이 이처럼 변모했을 것’이라는 걸 느낄 수 있는 장소입니다.

items.title: 65세 실외, 79세 실내… 나이 따라 낙상 장소 달라
items.snippet: 75세 김모씨는 집 근처 공원을 걷다가 산책로의 작은 턱에 발이 걸려 넘어졌다. 오른쪽 고관절이 골절돼 수술을 받고 병원에 입원하는 신세가 됐다. 하루 종일 누워 있는 시간이 많다 보니 근육이 확 줄었다. 부쩍 노쇠된 몸 상태가 됐다. 요즘 정형외과 병원에 가면 흔히 볼 수 있는 노년기 낙상 모습이다. 젊어서 넘어지는 것은 잠깐의 사고로 끝나지만, 노년기에 넘어지면 골절과 입원, 근육 감소, 보행 장애, 사회적 고립으로 이어진다. 심하면 평생 지켜온 독립적인 생활을 잃고 요양시설에 들어가야 하는 상황도 생긴다. 그래서 노년에 넘어지면 인생도 무너진다는 말이 나온다.

items.title: 잘 먹고 많이 움직이면 1년內 입원 경험 11%↓
items.snippet: 식사의 질이 높고 신체활동도 충분한 성인은 두 가지 모두 부족한 성인보다 최근 1년간 입원 경험이 있을 가능성이 11% 낮은 것으로 나타났다. 서울대병원 가정의학과 박민선 교수팀은 국민건강영양조사(2014~2021년) 자료를 활용해 성인 3만7059명의 식사의 질·신체활동과 입원 경험의 연관성을 분석했다. 연구팀은 식사의 질을 한국인 식생활평가지수(KHEI)로 평가해 중앙값을 기준으로 높음·낮음으로 나눴다. 신체활동은 걷기를 포함한 여가 시간 활동량이 주 150분(약간 숨이 찰 정도의 활동) 이상이면 활동군, 미만이면 비활동군으로 구분했다. 식사 질 높고 낮음, 활동량 많고 적음에 따라 4개 조합으로 나누고, 최근 1년간 입원 경험과 최근 2주간 외래 방문 경험을 비교했다.

items.title: 전립선암 제거 ‘앞’ 아닌 ‘뒤’로 했더니… 후유증 확 줄어
items.snippet: 초고령사회를 맞아 남성암 1위 전립선암, 요즘 전립선암 제거 수술은 거의 모두 로봇 수술로 한다. 기존에 배를 열고 하는 수술보다 정교한 로봇 손과 팔로 전립선을 세밀하게 제거할 수 있기 때문이다. 하지만 그래도 일부에서 수술 후 배뇨 장애가 발생하여 고생을 한다. 그런 배경 속에서 환자에게 수술 후 배뇨 기능을 잘 유지할 수 있도록 하는 ‘새로운’ 수술법이 주목받고 있다. 전립선 뒤쪽으로 접근해 암을 제거하는 이른바 후방 접근 로봇 전립선절제술이다. 가천대 길병원 비뇨의학과 김태범 교수팀은 이 수술을 집중적으로 시행하며 경험을 축적해 왔다. 올해 9월 기준으로 후방 접근 수술이 1000례에 육박한다. 이 수술을 받은 환자의 배뇨 기능 회복을 분석한 연구 2편을 길병원 박일우 교수 등이 최근 이탈리아에서 열린 유럽비뇨의학회 로봇비뇨기수술분과...

items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 대장 용종 제거후 추가 내시경 5년뒤 해도 돼
items.snippet: 대장암은 주로 폴립(용종)이란 작은 종양으로 시작하기에 건강검진을 통해 조기에 폴립을 찾아내고 제거하면 대장암 발생을 예방할 수 있다. 폴립 크기가 10㎜ 이상이거나, 개수가 3개 이상이거나, 낮게 깔리는 융모 형태로 자란 경우 등에서는 향후 대장암으로 발생할 가능성이 높기 때문에, 폴립 제거 후 3년 후 대장내시경 검사를 다시 받도록 추천한다. 최근 노르웨이와 스페인 연구팀은 폴립 제거 후 적절한 대장경 검사 시기가 언제인지를 조사하고, 그 결과를 세계 최고의 학술지 뉴잉글랜드 의학저널(NEJM)에 발표했다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [생활 속 경제] 기후 위기가 만든 새로운 바닷길… 유럽 가는 시간 30% 줄여준대요
items.snippet: Q. 지난 11일 북극 항로를 시험 운항한 컨테이너선이 부산으로 돌아왔다는 뉴스를 보았어요. 북극 항로가 무엇이고, 이 길이 열리면 어떤 점이 좋을까요? 북극 항로는 북극해를 가로질러 아시아와 유럽을 잇는 가장 짧은 뱃길입니다. 아시아에서 수에즈 운하를 거쳐 유럽으로 향하는 길은 약 2만㎞인데, 북극 항로의 길이는 약 1만 3000㎞에 불과해요. 우리가 흔히 보는 평면형 세계지도에서는 북극이 가장자리에 놓여 있어 이 길이 잘 보이지 않아요. 하지만 둥근 지구본을 위에서 내려다보면 북극해를 가로질러 두 대륙을 잇는 길이 보이죠.

items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach...

items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data s...

items.title: On-sky performance and prospects of near-infrared CMOS detectors in exoplanet detection: first year of SPIRIT
items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. items.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. Latent-space optimization in the PCA-reduced latent space with Bayesian optimization, evolutionary search, random search, and quasi-exhaustive search is demonstrated for a common-source voltage amplifier with NMOS input and resistive load, where the objective function is defined as a penalty for deviation from required circuit specifications. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. Gallium oxynitride (GaON) could connect the technologically important GaN and Ga2O3 systems, yet establishing a clear relation between its crystal structure, composition and bandgap remains challenging. Here we report the direct growth of crystalline spinel gamma-GaON films by nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed-laser deposition. Varying the nitrogen and oxygen supply yields monoclinic beta-Ga2O3, predominantly disordered films and crystalline spinel GaON. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: Thermal stability and structural ordering of thick Co$_2$MnAl films grown on MgO and Si substrates
items.abstract: While most studies on Co$2$MnAl (CMA) focus on the ultrathin regime for spintronic junctions, applications scaling with magnetic volume--such as Anomalous Nernst Effect (ANE) energy harvesters, integrated power inductors, and magnetic MEMS--require significantly thicker films. In this work, 750 nm thick CMA films were grown on MgO (001) and Si substrates to establish a roadmap for their thermal integration. Structural analysis reveals that B2 ordering is optimized on MgO at 600 $^\circ$C, which is important for functional devices. In contrast, samples on Si substrates exhibit a disorder transition toward the A2 phase, closely linked to diffusion-driven degradation processes. items.title: ARES: a plane-wave density-functional-theory code in Rust
items.abstract: ARES (Ab initio atomic mateRial modEling Software at JLU) is a plane-wave density-functional-theory (DFT) code written entirely in Rust as a layered 22-crate workspace. It supports norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method with the local-density approximation (LDA) and Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functionals, Γ-only and explicit k-point sampling, smearing and mixing, forces, stress, relaxation, band structures, densities of states (DOS) and dispersion corrections; execution is serial or MPI-distributed over k-point pools, band groups and plane-wave rows. The code's distinguishing engineering choice is its validation apparatus. items.title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
items.abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. Local overheating of the material increases the free-carrier density and conductivity, which in turn enhances the absorption of the incident radiation and further amplifies local heating and avalanche ionization. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. items.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
items.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. items.abstract: We present first-principles calculations of the electron-hole-pair creation energy in semiconductors and dielectrics, focusing in particular on AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2. We have employed density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the band structure, density-functional perturbation theory to obtain the phonon dispersion, and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) to calculate the electron energy loss function (via the dielectric function). We performed full-band Monte Carlo simulations of electron thermalization for energies up to ~100 eV and calculated the average energy required to excite an electron-hole pair. We calculated pair-creation energies of approximately 12.2, 6.5, 7.3, 3.10, and 16.7 eV/pair for AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2, respectively. items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. We analyze 107 measured DC transfer curves from 37 isolated IGZO transistors (W/L = 3/0.5 micrometers). Four gate-bias operating points inferred from the first sweep are evaluated on later sweeps of 35 devices. Device-resolved operating points reduce second-sweep across-device current standard deviation by 49.4-52.4%, yet retaining initial thresholds increases misclassified points from 37/140 to 55/140. Leave-one-device-out reference estimation gives 0/140 on the second sweep; freezing second-sweep thresholds yields 6/140 on the third. Sampling eight reference transistors on the third sweep gives a mean held-out error fraction of 0.15% over 2,000 selections, versus 4.33% with frozen thresholds on matched held-out devices. items.title: Stateless Stochastic Computing for Generative AI on Superconducting Logic: A Model-Hardware Co-Design
items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. items.title: Localized Joule heating and carbonization process optimization of 3D printed polymer structures for lab-on-CMOS applications
items.abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. Such high temperature is detrimental to the CMOS sensor circuits, causing severe degradation. We present a novel solution of localized Joule heating of these polymer nanostructures to achieve complete carbonization of the electrodes. Both analytical and COMSOL simulations guided the experiments to characterize the carbonization process conditions. items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. items.title: Quantum-vortex excitons beyond band topology
items.abstract: Optically exciting a typical low-dimensional semiconductor produces a nodeless \(s\)-type exciton as its lowest-energy bound state. Here, we explain how Coulomb phase matching stabilises a quantum-vortex exciton as the lowest bound state in flat Chern bands. Using a prototypical Yin--Yang kagome lattice, we demonstrate that increasing the spin--orbit coupling drives a transition of the lowest exciton from a quantum-vortex state to a zero-winding state, while leaving the band Chern numbers unchanged. We trace this behaviour to a gauge-invariant combination of exciton phase differences and Bloch-overlap phases that can reduce the Coulomb energy. By comparing states with identical wavefunction amplitudes, we isolate this phase contribution and show that it is sufficient to drive the reversal in exciton ordering. We classify exciton topology by the momentum-space wavefunction winding relativ...

items.title: Surface Physics of Low-Dimensional Pnictogen Chalcohalides and Its Impact on Photovoltaic Technologies

Efficient charge extraction depends critically on the band-edge alignment between the absorber and the charge-selective contacts, which is a surface property. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with device-level modelling to investigate the surface energetics and band alignments across the MChX family. An exhaustive sampling of crystal orientations, including low-symmetry facets, identifies the (011) and (010) surfaces as the most stable terminations in all eight compounds. items.abstract: Spatial defect signatures on wafer bin maps (WBMs) trace yield loss to specific process faults, yet supervised classifiers recognize only the defect types seen during training, and one-class detectors built on a single mechanism tend to capture either local structural deviations or global distributional violations, but rarely both. items.title: Ambipolar metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe2
items.abstract: When Coulomb interactions dominate kinetic energy, dilute two-dimensional carriers form a Wigner solid. Both its melting and disorder-driven localization can drive density-tuned metal-insulator transitions, but their relative roles and interplay have been debated for decades. Atomically thin semiconductors offer a new test because transport and scanning tunneling microscopy can probe the same material, yet poor contacts impede transport where correlations are strongest. Here we introduce contact-free radio-frequency reflectometry that senses sheet resistance through capacitive gate coupling. It resolves the electron and previously inaccessible hole transitions in the same bilayer MoSe2 device, whose carriers share disorder but not mass. items.title: MarketRank: ranking stocks by the stationary probabilities of a Markov chain over estimated money flows, with a topological landscape view
items.abstract: Every trading day, money leaves some stocks and moves into others. MarketRank asks where that money concentrates and how the concentration shifts over time. It treats the market as a Markov chain whose states are stocks. The chance of moving from one stock to another is the share of the first stock's outgoing dollars that goes to the second, and a stock's MarketRank score is its long run (stationary) probability in that chain, computed by damped power iteration on a sparse transition matrix. PageRank ranks web pages with the same idea, using links instead of dollars. Who sold what to buy what is not public, so the flows are estimated from daily prices and volumes with a correlation tilted gravity model, in a deterministic parallel C++ engine. items.title: Superconducting edge contact to a buried Ge quantum well
items.abstract: Semiconductor-superconductor hybrid systems form the basis for a broad range of quantum phenomena, such as Andreev bound states, topological superconductivity, and hybrid quantum Hall states. The performance of these hybrid systems can strongly benefit from the exceptional electronic properties of heterostructures with deeply buried quantum wells. However, establishing high-quality superconducting contacts to such quantum wells remains challenging. Here, we address this problem with an edge-contact approach that combines anisotropic dry etching to access the quantum well followed by wet etching for interface preparation. items.title: Squeezed light from a semiconductor amplifier
items.abstract: The possibility of generating light in a squeezed quantum state during saturated light amplification in a semiconductor amplifier is theoretically analyzed. Due to four-wave mixing process during amplification, weak components of the spontaneous emission of the medium with symmetric frequency shifts relative to the strong amplified wave acquire the quantum properties of two-mode squeezed light. The squeezing of quadrature components occurs in the range of frequency shifts of several GHz ($\sim$ the inverse relaxation time of the charge carrier density) and can reach 10 dB or more under optimal conditions. The formation of a two-mode squeezing phase facilitates the observation of the squeezing effect, in which a strong wave, playing the role of a local wave, exhibits quadrature noise suppression without additional homodyne detection.

items.abstract: Understanding the formation and dynamics of two-exciton bound states (BSs) is crucial for harnessing multi-exciton phenomena and designing next-generation organic semiconductor materials. While various mechanisms such as intermolecular exciton-exciton interactions or multi-level intramolecular configurations can generate these BSs, a fundamental understanding of their underlying lattice dynamics remains a key challenge. Within this context, the Merrifield exciton model stands out as a premier framework for capturing the intricate quantum mixing between single-site doubly-excited states and two-particle scattering continuum. In this work, by constructing a set of exact two-exciton Bloch states and applying a plane-wave ansatz to treat the resulting inhomogeneous tridiagonal matrices, we provide a complete, rigorous solution to the two-exciton problem in a finite-size Merrifield chain. items.title: Sparse qubit operation in a 6$\times$6 quantum dot array
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires increasing the qubit count while maintaining high performance and connectivity. Semiconductor qubits have demonstrated high-fidelity operation, but growing the system size at sufficient connectivity remains challenging, such that scaling mainly occurred in one spatial direction to preserve access for control lines in the other. Here, we realise an approach that relaxes the requirements on fabrication and demonstrate a 6$\times$6 quantum dot array, defined by a shared barrier gate and individual plunger gates. The quantum dots are tuned through coherent spin shuttling over distances up to 5.2um into a sparse configuration of 10 simultaneously operated qubits, leaving space for shuttling connections. items.title: CacheFit: The Rising Cost of Cache Replacement and Constraint-Driven Redesign of Last-Level Cache Replacement Policies
items.abstract: The latency, power, and area costs of LLC replacement remain poorly explored not because simulators cannot be instrumented--event counters feeding a power model are routine--but because no cost model takes a replacement policy as input. CACTI and McPAT price regular structures, a cache or a core, not the small, oddly shaped arrays and dependent logic a policy is made of, and no event count reveals a victim-selection path's logic depth. Without a model, cost has never been an objective a policy search could optimize. In practice, a policy is first selected in simulation for its IPC, and its cost is reduced later in RTL, after the algorithm is fixed. Cost thus enters the design too late to shape it. items.abstract: Field-effect transistor (FET) layouts on exfoliated two-dimensional flakes are typically drawn by hand for each flake, placing contacts and gates to match its position and outline in optical micrographs. To our knowledge, no executable benchmark tests whether language-model agents can perform this flake-specific construction reliably. We introduce 2D-FET-Bench V2, a benchmark of 128 layout tasks built from microscopy-derived flake contours, including hole-containing flakes and multi-flake tasks. Each task supplies a textual device specification and contour coordinates. An agent generates typed polygon and path operations rendered to GDSII. A deterministic verifier checks geometric and structural requirements, and a separate integrity check verifies that the supplied contours remain unchanged. items.abstract: Process-induced warpage, ceramic stress and solder strain limit the reliability of insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) modules on direct-bonded copper (DBC) substrates. Surrogate-assisted design studies train regression models on finite-element analysis (FEA) databases, but rarely check the optimized designs against new FEA or report how surrogate error interacts with the optimizer. This paper builds and evaluates an open pipeline: an open-source process finite-element model, surrogates tuned by Simplified Swarm Optimization (SSO), multi-objective design search, FEA confirmation of selected designs and confirmation-driven infill. items.abstract: The optical properties of monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are strongly impacted by exciton-phonon coupling, especially inter-valley scattering in the case of tungsten-based materials. Considering exemplarily the resonance Raman profile of the A$_1$-mode in hBN-encapsulated monolayer WSe$_2$, we find that inter-valley scattering between the electronic K- and Q-valley leads to destructive interference between a first order and a third order Raman process. items.title: Vacancy aggregation enhances NV- spin coherence in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion study of multi-vacancy spin baths in semiconductors
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV-decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts t...

Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. First-principles theory of phonon renormalization from nonlinear electron-phonon interactions
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions renormalize phonon frequencies and lifetimes and are central to the dynamical properties of solids. While these effects are usually described within linear electron-phonon coupling, the role of nonlinear electron-phonon interactions for phonon properties remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study phonon renormalization arising from the long-range linear one-electron-one-phonon and the nonlinear one-electron-two-phonon interactions within a diagrammatic framework. We derive the corresponding self-energy diagrams, which depend on the chemical potential and temperature, and evaluate them from first principles for the two polar semiconductors LiF and KTaO$_3$. In both materials, the two interaction channels renormalize the phonon spectrum in qualitatively distinct ways. items.title: Compact Modeling of Oxide-Semiconductor, 2D Material, Carbon Nanotube, and Cryogenic Transistors with Experiment Verification
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified compact model for emerging transistor technologies, including oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (OSFETs), 2D material FETs (2DFETs), carbon nanotube FETs (CNFETs), and cryogenic MOSFETs. A unified charge-density formulation is developed to account for quantum confinement, trap charges, and band-tail states in channel charge calculations. A physics-based transport model is introduced to seamlessly capture carrier transport from the long-channel diffusive regime to the short-channel ballistic limit. Scaling models are incorporated to accurately describe 2D electrostatic effects. Cryogenic operation is modeled through the inclusion of band-tail states and temperature-dependent mobility and threshold voltage. The proposed model is validated against experimental data from the fabricated OSFETs with multiple channel lengths and published measurements of...

items.title: Optically Coupled Noise Spectroscopy Quantifies Defect Passivation in Monolayer MoS2 FETs
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are promising materials for electronic and photonic applications, yet the performance of chemical vapour deposition grown samples is severely limited by native sulphur vacancies that introduce mid-gap trap states, degrade carrier mobility, and elevate electrical noise. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. Thiol treatment reduces the sulphur vacancy concentration from 7% to 4%, reducing the free electron density. Electrically, it increases the device resistance 35-fold while restoring gate switching with an on/off ratio of 10^4 and improving field-effect mobility from 1 to 5 cm^2/Vs. Low frequency noise spectrosc...

items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q/V Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption
items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of qu...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Complex frequency-dependent quadrature squeezing in semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of quadrature squeezing in a quantum well laser based on a fully quantum Langevin approach. We compute the frequency-resolved squeezing map of the laser field and identify optimal squeezing curves, revealing, for the first time to our knowledge, both frequency-dependent squeezing and complex or hidden squeezing in a semiconductor laser. We further analyse the role of the linewidth enhancement factor (alpha-factor) in the emergence of these features. Our results establish semiconductor lasers as a platform for the generation of non-classical light and open new perspectives for their application in quantum communication and sensing.

items.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
items.abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structure...

items.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
items.abstract: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. The platform supports multilevel and multidimensional encoding by independently encoding information in fluorescence intensity and wavelength. A machine-learning-assisted super-resolution reconstruction protocol is developed to recover infor...

items.title: Anharmonic Quantum Transport Analysis of Thermal Transport Anomalies in Ultrathin Silicon Nanowires
items.abstract: Thermal transport in low-dimensional semiconductors is important for nanoelectronics, quantum devices, and thermoelectrics. Recent molecular dynamics (MD) studies reveal a nonmonotonic diameter dependence of thermal conductivity in ultrathin silicon nanowires (NWs), but classical MD is limited at low temperatures and under strong confinement. Here, we investigate this anomaly using anharmonic non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) simulations combined with density functional theory-trained neuroevolution potentials. All transport results are expressed as effective thermal conductivities ($κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$) for NW devices with a finite channel length of $L=10$ nm. At 300 K, $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ decreases with diameter to minima at 6.24 and 5.50 nm for [001]- and [110]-oriented NWs, respectively. At 10 K, the corresponding minima occur at 7.33 and 5.50 nm. items.title: Predictive Software Scheduling as an Early-Warning Hint Layer for Optical Engine Thermal Drift in Heterogeneous SoIC Packaging
items.abstract: As semiconductor scaling approaches the A16 / 2 nm node, the integration of co-packaged optics (CPO) through TSMC's Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE) architecture introduces critical thermal-optical coupling challenges. Micro-ring resonators embedded in the Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) layer are highly sensitive to temperature, with a wafer-level center wavelength deviation of merely +/-1.7 nm across a 300 mm wafer representing the platform's manufacturing control limit. To address this, we propose XRM-SSD V24, a physics-aware scheduling layer that models inference-load density 20-50 ms before execution and issues early-warning hints to the COUPE bias-control firmware, enabling pre-emptive thermal compensation. Simulation-based validation on a software emulation platform (physical characterization pending TSMC tape-out) over 90,000 inference steps yields a simulator-internal...

items.title: Speed Kills: Exploring Confused Deputy Attacks Through Edge AI Accelerators
items.abstract: AI Accelerators (AIAs) are specialized hardware, such as Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), that enable optimal and efficient execution of AI applications and on-device inference. The growing demand for AI applications has led to the widespread adoption of AIAs on edge and embedded devices. Unlike applications, AIAs are not bound by Operating System (OS) restrictions and have limited visibility into Application Processor (AP) security mechanisms (e.g., kernel versus application memory and process isolation). This semantic gap can lead to confused deputy vulnerabilities, where an AIA can be tricked by a malicious application into performing privileged operations on its behalf. In this paper, we conduct the first in-depth study of Confused Deputy Attacks (CDAs) using AIAs. We design DeputyHunt, a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted framework to extract CDA-relevant information for a given AIA...

items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models. Transaction-based network energy models were developed in 2009 to understand the evolution o...

items.title: Joint Architecture-Token-Bitwidth Multi-Axis Optimization of Vision Transformers for Semiconductor IC Packaging
items.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance in visual recognition, yet their deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments remains limited. The main challenges are their high computational cost, memory requirements, and energy consumption. While individual efficiency techniques such as neural architecture search (NAS), token compression, and low-precision inference have been extensively studied, most prior work targets only a single optimization axis, limiting overall deployment gains while preserving accuracy. In this paper, we present one of the first holistic frameworks that jointly optimizes three complementary axes: architecture, token, and bit-width. Specifically, the framework identifies compact backbones via Neural Architecture Search (AutoFormer), reduces information processing via token merging (ToMe), and accelerates per-operation execution via fp1...

items.title: Proximitized Topological Insulator Charge Island Fabricated via In Situ Multi-Angle Stencil Lithography
items.abstract: Hybrid superconductor-topological insulator (TI) nanostructures constitute a promising material platform for exploring proximity-induced superconductivity in systems with topologically protected surface states. A key obstacle has been the realization of clean and well-controlled superconductor-TI interfaces, as TI surfaces rapidly degrade under ambient conditions. Here, we introduce a fully in situ, multi-angle stencil lithography technique that enables the fabrication of proximitized charge islands in TIs. The approach combines selective area growth of (Bi,Sb)$_2$Te$_3$ nanoribbons with angle-controlled deposition of diffusion barriers, superconducting Al, and ultrathin oxide tunnel barriers, allowing scalable fabrication of hybrid nanostructures without post-growth processing.
